data.body:
## Summary
Closes #82.

Adds an immersive, step-by-step "Cooking Mode" for recipes, built so hands stay off the phone as much as possible while cooking, and structured so future voice/AI-driven control does not require a rewrite.

- **`CookingModeController`**: navigation state machine, free of SwiftUI. All navigation (next/previous/repeat/goTo) funnels through a single `handle(_:)` entry point — the seam a future voice recognizer, AI assistant, or gesture recognizer can call into.
- **`CookingModeView`**: full-screen, high-contrast, large-text single-step presentation with big Next / Previous / Repeat controls, per-step countdown timer (reuses the existing `CookingTimerStore`/`CountdownTimerView`), VoiceOver labels/hints/announcements, Dynamic Type friendly text, and disables the idle timer (`isIdleTimerDisabled`) so the screen doesn't auto-lock mid-step.
- **`CookingAssistantView` + `CookNowAIService.answerCookingQuestion`**: optional "Ask AI" modal for contextual step questions, demonstrating the AI hook without changing the core navigation flow.
- **`RecipeDetailView`**: adds an entry point into Cooking Mode (toolbar button + cover-page CTA), leaving the existing paged flow untouched.
- **Tests**: `CookingModeControllerTests` covers navigation clamping at both ends, repeat-without-moving, `startAt` clamping, and recipes with zero steps.

Touchless gestures and full voice-command recognition are intentionally left as follow-ups (per the issue's acceptance criteria) — the architecture above is designed to support them later without rewriting this flow.

## Goal
Add an A–Z index strip on the trailing edge of both **我的食材** and **购物清单** lists, matching the iOS Contacts alphabetic scroll bar. Tapping/dragging a letter jumps to the matching section.

## Implementation
- New `Components/AlphabeticIndex.swift`:

data.body:
## Why

The app record, distribution certificate and App Store provisioning profile all live under **team `9WZ247H2ZJ`** with bundle id **`com.nextradeai.ios.barry.DietExpert`** (the id Xcode Cloud originally set up, and the only one with an App Store Connect app record — App ID `6792149824`).

`main` however declared `com.nextradeai.ios.DietExpert` under team `LCPKCHA4B8`, which has **no** App Store Connect app record. As a result `main` could not be shipped to TestFlight without overriding the bundle id at build time. This PR makes the project self-consistent with what actually ships.

## Changes

- **`project.pbxproj`**: `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` → `com.nextradeai.ios.barry.DietExpert` (app) / `...barry.DietExpertTests` (tests); `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` → `9WZ247H2ZJ`.
- **App icon**: added the Nibble icon (`AppIcon.png` + single-size `Contents.json`). The icon set was empty, and App Store validation rejects builds with no icon (`CFBundleIconName` / missing 120×120·152×152).
- **fastlane**: added a `beta` lane (`cert` + `sigh` + `gym` + `pilot`) driven by an App Store Connect API key, using manual signing to avoid Xcode's automatic-signing "no account for team" failures on CI/CLI.
- **`.gitignore`**: ignore signing material (`*.p12`, `*.cer`, `*.certSigningRequest`, `*.mobileprovision`) and `.DS_Store`.

## Verification

Build **57** (v1.0) was built from this configuration and **successfully uploaded to TestFlight** (App Store Connect App `6792149824`).

> Note: the API key ID / issuer ID in `fastlane/Fastfile` are non-secret identifiers; the `.p8` private key is referenced by path outside the repo and is never committed.

## Summary

Second pass of the Nibble design adoption. #83 recolored the app at the token level; this PR makes the shared components structurally match the design system's primitives, so every screen using them gets consistent chips, tags, type, and macro colors.

## Changes

- **Theme** — new surface tokens `coralSoft` (peach-100), `jadeSoft` (sage-300), `paperTint` (cream-200 sunken surface), plus the design's **fixed macro palette** (protein = berry, carbs = sun, fat = blueberry), all with derived dark variants.
- **FilterChips (餐点库/周计划 filters)** — follow the Nibble **Chip** spec exactly: selected = peach-soft pill + 2px coral border + deep-coral bold text; unselected floats on white with a soft hairline. Press bounce included.
- **合成 tab chips** — the 台面 tray chips become Nibble **Tags** (sage-soft, borderless, dismissible — the design's "ingredient chip"), while the 冰箱 chips follow the **Chip** spec (selection = coral). This matches the design's explicit Chip-vs-Tag role split.
- **PageHeader** — page titles switch serif → rounded display type (Fredoka → SF Rounded); eyebrows become tracked caps in sage-600 (readable on cream).
- **MacroStatView** — macro labels get fixed-color dots; text stays ink for readability (per the design, colors identify macros, ink carries the numbers).
- **TodayView 全天合计 card** — restructured from side-by-side columns (which squeezed "68g 蛋白" into wrapping) to a stacked layout: macros row, divider, then 人均约 row. Radius 16.
- **Inner tiles** (DishRow, RecipeDetail macro strip / timer card, ReceiptScan photo) — sunken cream-200 fill and 16px continuous radius per the design's radius scale (16 inner / 22 cards).

Reskins the app to the **Nibble design system** (user-supplied `Nibble Design System.zip`): warm cream canvas (`#FFF7EF`), **coral** (`#FF7E5F`) as the primary/brand action color, **sage** as the healthy/fresh accent and selection color, warm ink text (never pure black), soft warm-tinted shadows, and rounded-everything.

## Summary

Every active-inventory ingredient — pantry rows in 我的食材 and the 冰箱/台面 capsule chips in 合成 — now behaves like a native interactive iOS component: long-pressing lifts it with the system context-menu animation (scale, shadow, dimmed background, haptic all OS-provided) and offers a destructive **已吃完** action that removes the item from stock.

## Implementation

- **New reusable modifier** `EatenContextMenu` (`Components/EatenContextMenu.swift`): native `.contextMenu` + `Button(role: .destructive)`, with `.contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, shape)` so rounded rows and capsule chips keep their own silhouette when lifted, `.sensoryFeedback(.success)` on commit, and a VoiceOver custom action so the operation doesn't require a visual long press. No `.onLongPressGesture` layered on top, so taps keep their existing behavior (edit sheet / selection toggle).
- **PantryView**: applies the modifier to each `PantryRow`; removal goes through `PantryStore.remove(_:)` by stable `UUID` inside `withAnimation`, gated by Reduce Motion.
- **CookNowView**: both fridge and tray chips get the menu with a `Capsule` lift shape; eating an item also drops it from the current 台面 selection.
- Persistence is unchanged: `PantryStore`'s `@Published items` `didSet` re-encodes to UserDefaults, so the change survives relaunch and all observing views (including empty states) update immediately.

Out of scope by design: ShoppingView (things to buy), ReceiptScanView lines (pre-inventory), RecipeDetailView ingredient lists (read-only recipe text).

## Testing

Adds a reusable project skill `temp-view` that codifies the "make a temp view" workflow we just used for the cooking animation / spark.

**Trigger:** when you say "做 temp view", "temp view", "让我先预览", "preview the options", "give me variants to choose", etc.

**What it does (3 phases):**
1. **Build** a throwaway in-app lab screen — one SwiftUI file with segmented-button pickers + live previews for 3–4 variants per visual dimension, using the app's design system.
2. **Preview** — add a temporary 预览 tab, build/launch, push so you can tap through it in the sim or on your iPhone; then you reply with your picks (e.g. "动画=1, 火花=1"). No implementation until you choose.
3. **Apply & clean up** — port the chosen variant into the real code, delete the temp view + tab, and collapse history so the final PR diff has no preview scaffolding; then build + test.

Tuned to this repo's conventions (synchronized folder groups so new files auto-compile, `Theme`/`cardStyle`/`PageHeader`, iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 sim, deployment target 26.5 so all modern SwiftUI APIs are available).

data.body:
Adds voice entry to the pantry: tap the mic, speak "我有鸡蛋、西兰花、两块鸡胸…", and the transcript becomes structured, editable pantry entries. All speech-to-text goes through the OpenAI Whisper API (no local `SFSpeechRecognizer`), which handles mixed 中文/English well.

### Flow
Mic → `AVAudioRecorder` (m4a) → Whisper `/v1/audio/transcriptions` → chat-completions JSON parse → confirm/edit screen → `PantryStore.addAll`.

### Changes
- **`Services/OpenAIService.swift`** — shared client. `transcribe(audioURL:)` (Whisper multipart upload) and `parsePantryItems(fromTranscript:)` (chat-completions, `response_format: json_object`, `gpt-4o-mini`, temp 0). Key read from Keychain per-call.
- **`Services/KeychainService.swift`** — stores the OpenAI key in the Keychain; nothing lands in UserDefaults or source.
- **`Services/PantryVoiceParser.swift`** — network-free prompt + decoding. Maps group tokens (english + chinese raw values, fallback `.vegetable`), tolerates code fences/prose around the JSON. Isolated so it's unit-testable without a live call.
- **`Services/AudioRecorder.swift`** — `AVAudioRecorder` wrapper, mono 16 kHz AAC.
- **`Features/PantryVoiceInputView.swift`** — record → transcribe → confirm/edit UI, with an inline API-key entry fallback when no key is set.
- **`Features/PantryView.swift`** — mic button in toolbar and empty state.
- **`project.pbxproj`** — `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (Debug + Release).
- **`DietExpertTests/PantryVoiceParserTests.swift`** — parser coverage (decode, group mapping, fence tolerance, empty-name/unit handling, error cases).

### Group token mapping
```swift
PantryVoiceParser.group(from: "蛋白")          // .protein
PantryVoiceParser.group(from: "fruitnutdairy") // .fruitNutDairy
PantryVoiceParser.group(from: "mystery")       // .vegetable (fallback)
```

### Cost
Whisper `whisper-1` bills at **$0.006 / minute** of audio (rounded to the nearest second); the `gpt-4o-mini` parse is a fraction of a cent per list.

### Notes for review
- This branch did not yet contain the "shared OpenAI client + key management" prerequisite the issue lists as a blocker, so a focused version of it is introduced here alongside the feature; worth deciding whether it should later be reconciled with a broader client.
- The parser is validated on Linux via `swiftc`; the full app build + tests run on the macOS CI runner.

data.body:
Bridges the pantry inventory (#21/#22) and the recipe library so users see what they can cook now: recipes ranked by ingredient coverage, missing items shown as chips and addable to the shopping list in one tap.

## Changes

- **`Features/CookNowEngine.swift`** — pure, side-effect-free enum (mirrors `Nutrition`) that scores recipes against the pantry:
  - Splits into **现在能做 / Cook now** (nothing missing) and **差一两样 / Almost there** (≤2 missing); anything worse is hidden.
  - Coverage % (5/6 → 83), sorted fullest-first / fewest-missing-first.
  - Token-matches compound names (`生菜、番茄` ↔ pantry `番茄`; `熟鸡胸(切片)` ↔ `鸡胸`) and treats `.seasoning` as always on-hand so oil/salt don't block a dish.
- **`Features/CookNowView.swift`** — renders both tiers with coverage %, missing-ingredient chips (chip flips to a checkmark once added), and navigation into `RecipeDetailView`. Reached from a card on the Pantry tab.
- **`ShoppingStore.swift`** — adds a persisted `custom: [Ingredient]` list (`addCustom`/`removeCustom`/`hasCustom`, key `liangren.shopping.custom.v1`) plus injectable `defaults`; `prune(keeping:)` never drops custom names.
- **`ShoppingView.swift`** — folds custom items into the grouped list, removable via context menu.
- **`ContentView.swift` / `PantryView.swift`** — hoists `PantryStore` + `ShoppingStore` to `ContentView` and shares them, so items added in Cook Now surface live in the Shopping tab.
- **Tests** — `CookNowEngineTests` (tiers, seasoning handling, compound matching, rounding, sorting) and `ShoppingStoreTests` (custom add/dedupe/remove/prune/persistence).

```swift
let ranking = CookNowEngine.rank(recipes: RecipeBook.recipes, pantry: pantry.items)
// ranking.cookNow    -> [清蒸鲈鱼 (100%), ...]
// ranking.almostThere -> [黑椒鸡胸杂蔬 missing: [鸡胸肉], ...]
```

## Deferred

The optional **AI substitution / new-recipe layer** and **save-as-custom-recipe (#26)** are not included — they depend on LLM/API-key infrastructure and a custom-recipe store that don't yet exist in the repo. This PR delivers the local ranking + shopping integration (the two testable acceptance criteria); the AI layer can sit on top of `CookNowEngine` once that infra lands.

## Notes for reviewers

- Coverage intentionally excludes seasonings; the denominator is "required" (non-seasoning) ingredients. Adjust `assumeAvailable` in `rank(...)` if that heuristic should change.
- iOS build/tests run on macOS CI only; logic here was type-checked and exercised via a standalone harness against the real recipe data.

data.body:
Recipes were entirely hard-coded in `RecipeBook`. This adds user-created recipes (name, emoji, macros, ingredients, steps with optional timers) with create/edit/delete, persisted on disk — kept intentionally low-key so the curated seed recipes remain the primary content.

## Data & lookup
- `RecipeStore` (new) — `ObservableObject` persisting custom recipes as JSON in UserDefaults (`liangren.customrecipes.v1`), injectable defaults for tests, following the `PlanStore`/`PantryStore` pattern.
- It mirrors into a new static `RecipeBook.customRecipes` registry, so the app-wide `RecipeBook.recipe(_:)` lookup resolves custom recipes with **no call-site changes** — planner, shopping aggregation, and `Nutrition.sum` participate automatically.
- `Recipe.isCustom` distinguishes editable user recipes from read-only seeds via the `custom-` id prefix.

```swift
static func recipe(_ id: String) -> Recipe? {
    recipes.first { $0.id == id } ?? customRecipes.first { $0.id == id }
}
```

## UI
- `RecipeEditorView` (new) — create/edit/delete form: name, emoji, accent swatch, category, multi-select slots & goal tags, servings, macros, blurb, add/removable ingredients, and steps with optional per-step timers (minutes → seconds).
- `LibraryView` — low-key `+` toolbar entry and a separate "我的菜谱" section; custom cards expose a per-card `⋯` menu for 编辑/删除. Seed grid unchanged and read-only.
- `ContentView` — holds the shared `RecipeStore` so custom recipes are loaded at launch (before any tab that reads them).

## Tests
- `RecipeStoreTests` — CRUD, persistence across restart, `isCustom`, and `RecipeBook` lookup + nutrition integration (serialized suite, per-test UserDefaults suite).

## Notes for reviewers
- Custom recipe ids use a `custom-` prefix; seed recipes are never routed to the editor.
- `RecipeBook.customRecipes` is a static mirror kept in sync by `RecipeStore`; the store is the source of truth. A single shared store instance backs all `LibraryView` entry points to avoid divergent state.

data.body:
The shopping list was derived entirely from the week plan, with no way to add real-world extras (paper towels, a soy-sauce refill, fruit). This adds free-form custom items that persist independently of the plan.

### Changes

- **`CustomShoppingItem` model** (`Models.swift`) — `name` + optional `amount` + `group`. Exposes a namespaced `checkKey` (`"custom:<uuid>"`) so a custom entry never collides with a generated ingredient of the same name.
- **`ShoppingStore`** — now persists `customItems` under a dedicated UserDefaults key alongside `checked`. Adds `addCustom`/`removeCustom` (delete also clears the item's checkmark) and makes `defaults` injectable. `prune(keeping:)` unions in custom check keys, so **plan regeneration never wipes custom items or their checked state**.
- **`ShoppingView`** — a "添加自定义" entry (pill button + toolbar `+`) opens a sheet (name / optional amount / group picker). Custom items render into their group section as checkable rows with per-item delete; progress totals include them.
- **`ShoppingStoreTests`** — covers add/toggle/remove, persistence across restart, and that `prune` keeps custom checks while dropping stale generated ones.

### Custom items survive plan changes

```swift
store.addCustom(CustomShoppingItem(name: "厨房纸", amount: "2卷"))
store.toggle(item.checkKey)
store.prune(keeping: [])        // simulate a plan that no longer references anything
// item and its checkmark remain
```

### Notes

- The store/model logic is Foundation-only and type-checks with swiftc; the iOS UI target builds via `xcodebuild` on macOS CI (not on the Linux agent), which is also why the CodeQL Swift scan could not create a database here.

The 打印 (Print) tab was named for printing but only offered a `ShareLink` with a plain-text summary. This replaces it with a real, multi-page PDF that doubles as the single shared artifact across iMessage/Mail/Notes/AirDrop and drives actual AirPrint.

### Export model
- New pure `MealPlanExport` (SwiftUI-free, unit-tested) builds the week grid, shopping list, and deduplicated per-recipe list in first-appearance order.
- Title derives from `Household.size` (dynamic, not hard-coded); filename is the human-readable `本周餐单.pdf`.
- Shopping-list grouping extracted into shared `ShoppingList.sections(for:)`, now used by both the export and `ShoppingView` (removes duplicated aggregation).

### PDF rendering (`MealPlanPDF.swift`, `#if canImport(UIKit)`)
- `MealPlanPDFRenderer` composes a swipeable A4 document with `ImageRenderer` + `UIGraphicsPDFRenderer`: **page 1** = compact, print-optimized week grid + two-column shopping list; **then one page per recipe** (cover + macros + ingredients + steps) — reads like a cookbook in Quick Look.
- `MealPlanPDFFile: Transferable` (PDF `DataRepresentation` + `suggestedFileName`) so one `ShareLink` surfaces iMessage, Mail, Notes, AirDrop, Files, and Print.
- `MealPlanPrinter.presentPrintDialog` wires `UIPrintInteractionController` for AirPrint, fed the same PDF.

### PrintView
- Shares the PDF and prints the same artifact; rendering is deferred so the tab shows a placeholder rather than blocking on appear, and regenerates on plan/goal/servings changes.

```swift
struct MealPlanPDFFile: Transferable {
    let data: Data
    let fileName: String
    static var transferRepresentation: some TransferRepresentation {
        DataRepresentation(exportedContentType: .pdf) { $0.data }
            .suggestedFileName { $0.fileName }   // 本周餐单.pdf
    }
}
```

### Tests
- `MealPlanExportTests` covers dynamic household title, filename, day/slot coverage, recipe dedup order, shopping parity, and the empty-plan case.

Out of scope per the issue: no PowerPoint/Keynote or image-card export — PDF is the only artifact. Notes integration is share-sheet only (no public write API).

data.body:
Recipe cards and covers used an emoji on a flat accent color as the food image. This adds bundled-photo support with the emoji as fallback, and a reusable pipeline so future custom recipes can generate their own photos.

### Changes

- **`RecipePhoto` view** (`Components/RecipePhoto.swift`): single entry point for recipe imagery — shows the bundled photo when present, else the emoji-on-accent placeholder.
- **Naming convention** (`Models.swift`): `Recipe.photoAssetName` → `photo-<id>`; `recipe.bundledPhoto` resolves the `UIImage` or `nil`.
- **Wiring**: `RecipeCard` banner and `RecipeCover` header now route through `RecipePhoto` (card clips to its 92pt banner; cover shows a rounded 200pt photo).
- **Assets**: `Assets.xcassets/RecipePhotos/` image-set scaffolding for all 17 seed recipes (ids verified against `RecipeBook.swift`), ready to receive PNGs.
- **Pipeline** (`Scripts/generate_recipe_photos.py`): reads recipes from `RecipeBook.swift`, generates a photo per recipe via the OpenAI Images API, and writes it into the matching image set. Handles both `b64_json` and `url` responses. Documented in `docs/recipe-photos.md`.
- **Test**: covers the `photo-<id>` convention across all seed recipes.

```swift
// Card / cover both render through one fallback-aware view:
RecipePhoto(recipe: recipe, emojiSize: 40)
// recipe.bundledPhoto == UIImage(named: "photo-\(recipe.id)")  // nil → emoji
```

### Note

Image sets ship empty — actual photos require running the pipeline with an `OPENAI_API_KEY` (network access unavailable in this environment). Until populated, every recipe shows the emoji fallback; running the script bundles photos with no further code changes.

data.body:
The Today tab derived the current day/meal-slot from `Date.currentSlot`/`todayKey` at render time only, so an app left open (or suspended) across lunch→dinner or past midnight kept showing a stale day/meal. It also crammed four competing blocks onto the landing page, burying the one number that matters (per-person kcal vs. goal).

## Time refresh
- **`Theme.swift`**: `Date.dayKey`/`slot`/`greeting` now take a `Date` (testable, clock-driven); the old static accessors remain as thin wrappers. New `Date.nextBoundary(after:)` returns the next slot/greeting/midnight crossing.
- **`TodayClock.swift`** (new): `ObservableObject` publishing `now` with derived `day`/`slot`/`greeting`; `refresh()` re-reads the time and re-arms a one-shot timer that fires exactly on the next boundary.
- **`TodayView.swift`**: refreshes the clock on `onAppear`, `scenePhase == .active`, `NSCalendarDayChanged`, and `significantTimeChangeNotification` — covering foreground, midnight, and meal-boundary crossings.

## Homepage redesign
- Per-person **kcal-vs-goal badge** in the header, color-coded 偏低/合适/偏高 — the key number is visible without scrolling.
- Focused "now" card: current meal's dishes plus a peek at the next scheduled meal (`接下来 · …`).
- Compact day overview with the current meal highlighted.
- Full macro breakdown (whole-table + per-person) and the goal note moved into a collapsible `营养明细` `DisclosureGroup`, removing the previous large stat block.

## Tests
- `TodayScheduleTests`: slot hour-bands, weekday→`DayKey`, next-boundary crossings (slot + midnight rollover), and `TodayClock` with an injected time.

```swift
// Boundary logic is now pure and testable:
Date.slot(for: date(2026, 7, 5, 12))        // .lunch
let next = Date.nextBoundary(after: date(2026, 7, 5, 12))
Date.slot(for: next)                         // .snack (14:00)
```

Note: iOS build + `xcodebuild test` run in CI (macOS-only); the Foundation-level logic was verified locally with `swiftc`.

data.body:
The recipe library only exposed category/goal filter chips. This adds search, sorting, a right-edge index scrubber, and a language toggle, with all logic extracted into a testable engine.

### `LibraryEngine.swift` (new — pure, view-agnostic)
- **`filter`** — search over `name`, `nameEn`, and ingredient names (case- & diacritic-insensitive), composed with the existing category/goal filters.
- **`sort`** — `alphabetical` (pinyin for CN / A–Z for EN), `dateAdded` (stable seed order in `RecipeBook`, since the model has no timestamps), `kcal` (descending).
- **`sections`** — groups a sorted list into `(initial, recipes)` buckets for the index bar.
- **`RecipeLanguage`** / **`LibrarySort`** enums; `Recipe.displayName(_:)` and `Recipe.indexInitial(_:)`.

Pinyin initials come from Foundation's Latin transform, so no lookup table is needed:

```swift
source.applyingTransform(.toLatin, reverse: false)?
      .folding(options: .diacriticInsensitive, locale: Locale(identifier: "en_US"))
// 清蒸鲈鱼 -> "qing zheng lu yu" -> "Q";  "Steamed Sea Bass" -> "S"
```

### `LibraryView.swift`
- `.searchable` field, sort `Menu`, and a one-tap CN↔EN toggle in the header.
- Right-edge index bar (alphabetical sort only) scrolls to sections via `ScrollViewReader`; section headers rendered per initial.
- Language toggle drives display names, sort order, and index initials together; category/goal chips unchanged. Added empty state and language-aware accessibility labels.

### `RecipeCard.swift`
- Optional `language` param (defaults `.zh`) to render the active-language name.

### Tests
- `LibraryEngineTests` covers search variants, pinyin/A–Z initials, all three sort modes, and section coverage/ordering.

**Scope note:** ingredient search matches Chinese ingredient names; `Ingredient.nameEn` (flagged in the issue as coming from localization #11) is not yet in the model, so per-ingredient English search is out of scope here. Recipe-level `nameEn` search is supported.
data.title: Library: search, pinyin/A–Z index bar, sort dropdown, and CN/EN toggle

data.body:
The weekly planner's destructive actions — 清空 (clear week), 恢复推荐 (reset to seed), and 清空这天 (clear one day) — fired instantly with no confirmation and no way to recover a wiped plan. This adds a confirmation step and a time-boxed undo.

### `PlanStore` — in-memory undo
- Destructive methods (`clearAll`, `clear(day:)`, `resetToSeed`) now route through `applyDestructive(_:message:)`, which snapshots the current `WeekPlan` into a published `pendingUndo` before mutating.
- `undo()` restores the snapshot; `expireUndo()` discards it. The window auto-expires after `undoWindow` (5s) via a cancellable `DispatchWorkItem`, so a new action or a completed undo cleanly supersedes the previous one.

### UI wiring
- `PlannerView`: 清空 / 恢复推荐 now open `.confirmationDialog`s (destructive + cancel) instead of acting immediately; a bottom `safeAreaInset` surfaces the undo snackbar while `pendingUndo` is set.
- `DayPlanCard`: 清空这天 gets its own per-day confirmation dialog.
- New `UndoSnackbar` component — themed toast with a 撤销 action.

```swift
private func applyDestructive(_ next: WeekPlan, message: String) {
    let previous = plan
    plan = next
    pendingUndo = PlanUndo(message: message, previousPlan: previous)
    scheduleUndoExpiry()
}
```

### Tests
- `PlanStoreTests` covers snapshot/restore for each action, single-day restore, resetToSeed restoring a customized week, and expiry dropping the snapshot without mutating the plan.

Note: iOS build/tests run on macOS CI (xcodebuild); undo logic was additionally verified against a standalone Foundation harness.
data.title: Add confirmation dialogs + undo for destructive planner actions

data.body:
Shopping list ingredients were deduplicated by name but showed whichever recipe's amount was seen first — if eggs appeared in four recipes ("2 个", "1 个"…), the list still said "2 个". Quantities were silently wrong and ignored servings overrides.

### Changes

- **`Ingredient` gains structured `quantity` + `unit`** (`Models.swift`): auto-parsed from the existing free-text `amount` via `Ingredient.parseAmount`, so no recipe definitions change. Amounts without a leading number (`适量`, `一小把`, `少许`) stay unquantified and fall back to free text.
- **New `ShoppingList` aggregator** (`ShoppingList.swift`, Foundation-only): sums the same ingredient + unit across the week, scales quantities by per-recipe `ServingsStore` overrides, and tracks a dish count for unquantifiable items. Dependencies are injected (plan / recipe lookup / servings) so it's testable without SwiftUI.
- **`ShoppingView` delegates to the aggregator** and renders `displayAmount`, observing `ServingsStore.shared` so overrides reflow the list.
- **Tests** (`ShoppingListTests.swift`): parsing, cross-recipe summing, servings scaling, and the free-text fallback.

### Behavior

`displayAmount` renders summed quantities, falling back to a dish count when unquantifiable:

```
鸡蛋   →  4个                    # 2个 (r1) + 1个×2 (r2, doubled via override)
葱     →  适量 ×2 道菜
盐     →  2g + 适量 ×1 道菜       # mixed quantifiable + free-text
```

### Notes

- `parseAmount` handles trailing notes (`1 条(约 500 g)` → `1 条`) and leading text (`约 28 g(一小把)` → `28 g`).
- Same-name ingredients recorded in different units are summed per unit and joined (`… + …`), rather than silently collapsed.
data.title: Merge shopping list quantities across recipes (structured amounts)

data.body:
The app assumed exactly two diners everywhere ("N人健康餐单" copy, per-person figures), with no way for users to change it. This adds a persisted household-size setting that all diner-derived copy and figures read dynamically.

### Changes

- **`SettingsStore`** (new) — `ObservableObject` singleton managing `householdSize`, persisted to UserDefaults under `Household.sizeKey`. Injectable `defaults` for tests (matches `PlanStore`); a private `@Published` backing store clamps to range on assignment.
- **`Household` enum** — Promoted to single source of truth: adds `range` (1–6), `defaultSize` (2), and a shared `clamp(_:)` helper; `size(in:)` clamps stored values on read.
- **`SettingsView`** (new) — 设置 page with a 1–6 人 `Stepper`, presented as a sheet from a new `gearshape` toolbar button in `TodayView`.
- **`PrintView`** — Title reads `settings.householdSize` instead of a static value; observing views re-render on change.
- **Tests** — `SettingsStoreTests` covers default (2), persistence across restart, and clamping of out-of-range assignments and stored values.

### Notes for reviewers

- Default stays **2**, so existing users see no change.
- `Nutrition.perPerson` remains servings-based (one serving of each dish, per the existing #7 rework and the "人均为每道菜一人份之和" footnote) rather than dividing the table total by household size — the setting drives menu copy and, going forward, shopping quantities. Flagging in case a household divisor was expected here instead.

```swift
enum Household {
    static let range = 1...6
    static let defaultSize = 2
    static func clamp(_ value: Int) -> Int { min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound) }
    static func size(in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Int {
        let stored = defaults.integer(forKey: sizeKey)
        return stored > 0 ? clamp(stored) : defaultSize
    }
}
```

data.body:
The app carried 5–6 tab-bar tabs including a low-value 打印 destination, while offering **no place to configure the app** (household size, goal, default servings). This reworks the information architecture: export/share becomes an action on the week plan, and a dedicated Settings page centralizes preferences.

## Changes

- **Merge 打印 → 周计划**: removed the standalone Print tab; `PlannerView` now exposes export/share as a toolbar action (`square.and.arrow.up`) that presents the existing `PrintView` (text share / AirPrint / save via the iOS share sheet) in a sheet.
- **Weekly calendar**: added `WeekStrip` — a horizontal 7-day overview with today highlighted, per-day kcal at a glance, and tap-to-jump to a day's card (`ScrollViewReader`). Dropped the inline goal picker to cut clutter.
- **Settings (设置)**: new `SettingsView` for household size, goal, and default servings, backed by a new `SettingsStore` (UserDefaults-persisted, injectable `defaults:` for tests). Reached via a gear button in the 今日 nav bar, keeping the tab bar at 5 tabs.
- **Dynamic diner count**: `Household.size` and `SettingsStore` share one UserDefaults key, so 人均 copy tracks the setting; default stays **2** so existing users see no change.
- **Tests**: `SettingsStoreTests` covering defaults, persistence across restart, and shared-key behavior.

`SettingsStore` and `Household.size` read the same key, so the stored default keeps behavior stable:

```swift
static let householdKey = "liangren.household.v1"

enum Household {
    static let sizeKey = SettingsStore.householdKey   // shared key
    static var size: Int {
        let stored = UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: sizeKey)
        return stored > 0 ? stored : SettingsStore.defaultHouseholdSize  // 2
    }
}
```

## Notes for reviewers

- The `liangren.*` UserDefaults key prefix is kept for consistency with `PlanStore`/`ServingsStore`/`PantryStore` and the pre-existing household key.
- Settings uses a **gear button** rather than a 6th tab, since a 我的食材 tab was added after the issue was written; this honors the "5 or fewer tabs" criterion. Open to switching to a dedicated 设置 tab if we'd rather drop another.
- Goal editing moved out of `PlannerView` into Settings; `TodayView` still displays it read-only.
data.title: Navigation overhaul: fold Print into 周计划 export, add Settings page, sharpen the weekly calendar

data.body:
Adds a **P0 share button** so users can send scanned-receipt output and per-step cooking images through the standard iOS share sheet (iMessage / Mail / Notes / AirDrop / Save to Files). The receipt scan (#22) and AI step-image generators live in separate issues; this wires their outputs to a single sharing path. Where a generator doesn't exist yet, the path renders the outputs available today, so future generators can feed straight in.

## Changes

- **`Services/ShareExport.swift`** — Foundation-only helper for sanitized, human-readable filenames (`番茄炒蛋 - 第 1 步.png`, `番茄炒蛋 - 全部步骤.pdf`, `小票 2026-07-05.png`, `小票清单 2026-07-05.pdf`). Illegal chars → spaces, whitespace collapsed, empty → fallback stem.
- **`Components/ShareSheet.swift`** — the single share path. `ShareSheet` wraps `UIActivityViewController`; `ShareRenderer` renders SwiftUI cards to PNG and multi-page PDF temp files with those filenames.
- **`Features/RecipeDetailView.swift`** — share menu exporting the current cover/step as PNG or all steps as one PDF, via fixed-layout `RecipeCoverShareCard` / `RecipeStepShareCard` (avoids `ScrollView`, which has no intrinsic size for `ImageRenderer`).
- **`Features/ReceiptScanView.swift`** + new **“小票” tab** — attach a receipt photo (`PhotosPicker`) and item list; share the image and/or parsed list (PDF), or both with one captured timestamp.
- **`DietExpertTests/ShareExportTests.swift`** — covers sanitization, fallbacks, and filename formats.

Sharing routes through file URLs so recipients see a friendly name and need no app to view:

```swift
let url = ShareRenderer.pngURL(
    from: RecipeStepShareCard(recipe: recipe, step: step, index: page),
    name: ShareExport.stepImageName(recipe: recipe.name, step: page)
) // → ShareSheet(items: [url])
```

## Notes
- Both `pdfURL` overloads are used: `[UIImage]` for the all-steps PDF, `[some View]` for the single receipt-list card.
- Scope is share-only; `ReceiptScanView` owns just the share step, ready to consume #22's scanned image + parsed items.

data.body:
## Summary
The app rendered with a fixed light-only palette, so on devices set to Dark appearance, text colors fell back to `.primary` (white) over hardcoded light backgrounds — making the Print/Export screen and other text unreadable, and the recipe thumbnail tag pills invisible (white text on a white capsule).

This PR makes the app follow the **system** Light/Dark setting.

## Changes
- **`Theme.swift`**: palette is now appearance-adaptive. Added a `Color(light:dark:)` initializer backed by a `UIColor` dynamic provider, and gave every token a tuned dark variant while preserving the warm "paper" / jade / amber identity.
- **`RecipeCard.swift`**: recipe thumbnail tag pills (增肌 / 减脂 / 均衡) previously used default `.primary` text on `.white` — invisible in dark mode. They now use fixed `Theme.tagChip` / `Theme.tagInk` so the chip stays a light pill with dark text over the (fixed-color) thumbnail in both appearances.

## Verification
- `xcodebuild ... clean build` succeeds for the iOS Simulator.
- Manually verified in the simulator under **Dark** appearance across Today, Shopping list, More menu, and Library — text, cards, accents, and tag pills are all readable.
- Light appearance is unchanged from the original design.
data.title: Add system-driven dark mode support

Delivers the four open issues in the **P0 · OpenAI pantry scan + step images** milestone (#41, #22, #42, #43). These are interdependent (#41 is the client/key foundation the rest build on), so they land together in one PR rather than one PR per issue.

### #41 — OpenAI key management + shared client
- `KeychainService`: Keychain-backed `KeyStore` (never UserDefaults, never committed); `InMemoryKeyStore` for tests/previews.
- `OpenAIService.shared`: one thin client for vision + image generation — central base URL, auth header, error/rate-limit handling, masked-key display, per-call cost notes.
- `SettingsView` (new **设置** tab) to paste/replace/clear the key; `APIKeyMissingView` for graceful degradation when no key is set. Non-AI features are unaffected.

### #22 — Receipt scanning → pantry
- `ReceiptScanView`: pick a receipt image → vision call → `ReceiptParser` produces structured `PantryItem`s (tolerant of code-fenced/prose-wrapped JSON and string quantities; CN/EN name normalization via `PantryClassifier`) → editable confirmation list with unmatched rows flagged → insert into `PantryStore`. Entry point added to the Pantry toolbar.

### #42 — AI per-step cooking images
- `StepImageService` + `StepImageCache`: fixed style preamble shared across all steps, **explicit** generate button (not on-view, to control cost), on-disk cache keyed by recipe id + step index, emoji fallback while generating / on failure / no key.

### #43 — Sharing
- `ShareTempFile` / `ShareLink` reusable path + `ShareNaming` for human-readable filenames, wired into the receipt result (image + parsed list) and each recipe step image.

### Tests
- swift-testing coverage for the pure logic: parser, classifier, prompt/cache keys, share filenames, key masking, and request/response builders.

### Notes for reviewers
- The coding agent works in a single PR and cannot open multiple PRs; all milestone issues are delivered here. Milestone issue #21 (pantry core) was already merged.
- The iOS build + unit tests run on the macOS CI workflow, currently gated as `action_required` pending maintainer approval to run.

> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>[P0] OpenAI API key management + shared client service</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## EN
> **Priority: P0.** Foundation for every AI feature in this milestone. Today the app has no way to authenticate to any AI provider. This issue adds user-supplied **OpenAI** API-key entry + secure storage + one shared client. **OpenAI only** — no Claude/other providers.
> 
> **Requested:**
> - **Key entry UI**: a field to paste an OpenAI API key. Lives in a Settings section (the Settings page from lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39; if lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39 hasn't landed, ship a minimal standalone settings sheet so this issue stays independent).
> - **Secure storage**: store the key in the **Keychain**, never in UserDefaults and never committed. Provide clear/replace and a masked display.
> - **Shared `OpenAIService`**: one thin client used by all AI features — vision (receipt/image → structured JSON, lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#22) and image generation (per-step images). Central base URL, auth header, error/loading/rate-limit handling, and a single place to note per-call cost.
> - **Graceful absence**: if no key is set, AI features show a clear "add your OpenAI key" prompt instead of failing silently. Non-AI features keep working.
> 
> ## 中文
> **优先级:P0。** 本里程碑所有 AI 功能的基础。目前应用无法向任何 AI 提供方鉴权。本 issue 增加用户自填 **OpenAI** API key 的输入 + 安全存储 + 统一客户端。**仅支持 OpenAI**,不接入 Claude/其它。
> 
> **需求:**
> - **Key 输入界面**:粘贴 OpenAI API key 的输入框,放在设置区(来自 lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39 的设置页;若 lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39 未落地,先做一个独立的最小设置弹窗,保持本 issue 独立)。
> - **安全存储**:存进 **Keychain**,绝不放 UserDefaults、绝不提交仓库;支持清除/替换与掩码显示。
> - **统一 `OpenAIService`**:所有 AI 功能共用的瘦客户端——视觉(小票/图片→结构化 JSON,#22)与图像生成(分步配图)。集中 base URL、鉴权头、错误/加载/限流处理,并统一标注调用成本。
> - **无 key 时优雅降级**:未设置 key 时,AI 功能显示"请填入 OpenAI key"提示,不静默失败;非 AI 功能照常。
> 
> ## Acceptance criteria
> - [ ] User can paste, replace, and clear an OpenAI API key from a Settings surface
> - [ ] Key stored in Keychain (not UserDefaults, not in the repo)
> - [ ] A shared `OpenAIService` exposes vision + image-generation calls with error/loading handling
> - [ ] AI features degrade gracefully with no key set; non-AI features unaffected
> - [ ] No API keys committed anywhere
> 
> **Blocks:** lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#22, "AI per-step cooking images", "Share receipt + step images"
> **Related:** lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39 (Settings page hosts the field)
> **Files:** new `Services/OpenAIService.swift`, new `Services/Keychain.swift`, Settings surface (from lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#39 or a small standalone sheet)

> 
> **Implementation notes (per user decision):**
> - Use the **OpenAI Whisper API** (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`) for transcription — NOT the local `SFSpeechRecognizer`. Record with `AVAudioEngine`/`AVAudioRecorder`, upload the audio, get the transcript back (Whisper handles mixed Chinese/English well).
> - After transcription, parse the transcript into structured ingredients (an LLM call, e.g. GPT/Claude with a JSON schema, is more robust than regex for lists like "两块鸡胸").
> - API key management: keys must not be hard-coded in the app — plan for a lightweight proxy or user-supplied key in Settings; note per-minute transcription cost in the PR.
> - Pantry powers later features: "what can I cook" suggestions and shopping-list deduction.

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>[P0] AI-generated per-step cooking images (fixed style, OpenAI)</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## EN
> **Priority: P0.** Generate a cooking image for **each recipe step** with a **fixed, consistent visual style**, using the OpenAI image API. Distinct from lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#15 (which generates per-*recipe* cover photos, not per-step).
> 
> **Requested:**
> - For a given `RecipeStep`, build a prompt from the step title/content plus a **fixed style preamble** (same lighting/framing/art direction across all steps and recipes, so a recipe reads as one coherent set).
> - Call the **OpenAI image generation API** via the shared `OpenAIService`; **cache** the result to disk keyed by recipe id + step index so it is generated once, not on every view.
> - Show the image on the step page (replaces the current emoji header when a generated image exists); **emoji fallback** while generating / on failure / when no key.
> - Generation is **explicit** (a button, e.g. "生成配图"), not automatic on view, to control cost. Note per-image cost in the PR.
> 
> ## 中文
> **优先级:P0。** 用 OpenAI 图像 API 为**每个步骤**生成**固定统一风格**的配图。与 lihaoz-barry/ios-diet-expert#15(生成每道菜的封面图,非分步)不同。

data.body:
Photograph or pick a grocery receipt, extract its line items with a vision-capable LLM, review/edit them on a confirmation screen, and insert them into a pantry store. Introduces the pantry backing store (#21) this feature depends on.

### Pantry store
- `PantryStore` — `ObservableObject` over UserDefaults with an injectable `defaults:` (mirrors `PlanStore`). Re-buying the same name+unit merges quantities instead of duplicating rows.
- `PantryModels` — `PantryItem` and `ReceiptItem` (raw printed text + normalized name + quantity/unit/price + optional group; `group == nil` marks an unmatched line).
- `PantryView` + a new **食材库存** tab in `ContentView`.

### Receipt scanning
- `OpenAIReceiptScanner` (`ReceiptScanning` protocol) calls OpenAI vision (`gpt-4o`) with a strict JSON-schema prompt that maps abbreviations/brands → plain ingredient names (中/英). Supports image or text input.
- `ReceiptResponseParser` — networking-free decoder; strips ```json fences/prose and accepts numbers as JSON numbers or strings (`"2.5 kg"`). Isolated so it's unit-testable.
- `ReceiptTextRecognizer` — optional on-device `VNRecognizeTextRequest` OCR; `ReceiptScanModel` tries text-only first and falls back to uploading the image (cost saver).
- `IngredientMatcher` — bilingual keyword table placing items on a pantry shelf; returns `nil` (flagged for review) when uncertain.

### Confirmation UI
- `ReceiptScanView` — `PhotosPicker` → scan → editable rows; unmatched items flagged (amber) and require a category before insertion.

### API keys
- `APIKeyStore` keeps the user-supplied key in the **Keychain only** — nothing committed to the repo; an in-app editor lets users paste/clear it.

The confirmation flow keys off the matcher, e.g.:

```swift
let items = try ReceiptResponseParser.parse(modelReply)   // classifies via IngredientMatcher
model.unmatchedCount                                       // → flagged rows the user must categorize
pantry.add(receiptItems: model.items)                      // insert confirmed lines
```

### Notes
- Files auto-compile via the project's `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup`; no `project.pbxproj` edits needed.
- Chinese punctuation follows the existing half-width-colon convention (e.g. `PrintView` `Text("目标:\(…)")`).
- Camera/photo capture uses `PhotosPicker`, so no new Info.plist usage strings are required.
- Tests added: `PantryStoreTests`, `ReceiptParsingTests` (parsing, CN/EN matching, unmatched flagging, OpenAI envelope).

Closes #36
Closes #37

> Both infra changes in one PR at the user's request (tests + the CI that runs them).

## Changes

### Unit tests (#36)
- **New `DietExpertTests` target** (Swift Testing, hosted in the app) added to `DietExpert/DietExpert.xcodeproj` — 14 tests across:
  - `NutritionTests`: macro sums over known seed recipes, unknown-id handling, day-plan aggregation.
  - `PlanStoreTests`: seed week, add/remove/clear/reset semantics, persistence round-trip across store instances.
  - `CookingTimerTests`: wall-clock `remaining(at:)` math (running, past-end clamping, paused freeze), store default-timer vending.
- **Testability tweak**: `PlanStore` now accepts an injectable `UserDefaults` (default `.standard` — app behavior unchanged). Each test uses a throwaway suite, so runs are deterministic and never touch real app data.
- Per-person math tests intentionally deferred: PR #34 replaces that API; tests for it (and `ServingsStore`/`ShoppingStore`) should be added once #34/#35 merge.

### CI (#37)
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: on every PR to `main` and push to `main`, runs `xcodebuild test` on a `macos-26` runner (Xcode 26.x preinstalled), iPhone 17 simulator, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` — **no Apple Developer account or signing assets required**.
- **Shared scheme committed** (`xcshareddata/xcschemes/DietExpert.xcscheme`, with the test target wired into the Test action). The scheme previously existed only in `xcuserdata` (gitignored), so a fresh CI checkout would have had nothing to build.
- `concurrency` cancellation + 30-min timeout to conserve macOS minutes (billed 10× on private repos).

## ⚠️ One manual step to make CI blocking
The workflow runs automatically, but to make a red build **prevent merging**: Settings → Branches → add a branch protection rule for `main` → "Require status checks to pass" → select **Build & test (iOS Simulator)** (appears in the list after this PR's first run). Note: the three currently open PRs (#33/#34/#35) predate this workflow — update them (or close/reopen) to trigger their first CI run once protection is on.

## Verification
- `xcodebuild test` locally with the exact CI invocation: **TEST SUCCEEDED, 14/14 passed** on iPhone 17 Pro simulator.
- Conflict preflight (`git merge-tree`) against open PR branches #33, #34, #35: all OK.

Closes #8

## Changes
- **New `ShoppingStore`** (`DietExpert/DietExpert/ShoppingStore.swift`): holds the checked-item set, persisted to UserDefaults on every change, loaded on init.
- **`ShoppingView`** swaps its view-local `@State` set for a `@StateObject ShoppingStore`, so "already bought" progress survives the app being killed in the supermarket.
- **Invalidation**: checkmarks are pruned to the current ingredient list on appear and whenever the week plan changes — an item removed from the plan disappears (its stale checkmark is dropped), and newly added items start unchecked. The progress bar counts only checkmarks that are actually on the list.

## Why UserDefaults
Per the issue's request to evaluate persistence options: this is small, temporary state (a set of ingredient-name strings). UserDefaults matches the existing `PlanStore`/`CookingTimerStore` pattern in the repo; SwiftData would add schema/migration overhead with no benefit at this size. If the app later migrates to SwiftData for recipes (#26), this store is a 40-line file to swap.

data.body:
Closes #7

## Changes
- **Per-person math fixed** (`Theme.swift`): `Nutrition.perPerson` no longer halves the day total. It now sums one serving of each dish — `macros ÷ recipe.servings` per dish — so a 420 kcal single-serving breakfast counts as 420 kcal per person, not 210. Rounding happens once at the end (accumulated in `Double`), not per dish.
- **Servings editable per recipe** (new `ServingsStore.swift` + stepper on the recipe cover in `RecipeDetailView.swift`): each recipe keeps its default `servings`; the user can override it (e.g. double batch). Overrides persist in UserDefaults (matching the `PlanStore` pattern), and the cover's macro tiles plus all whole-table totals (Today / Planner / Print) scale by the batch factor. Per-person figures intentionally don't change with a batch override — cooking more of the same dish feeds more people, it doesn't change one person's plate.
- **No hard-coded diner count**: new `Household.size` (UserDefaults-backed, default 2) replaces the "两人健康餐单 / 主菜多为 2 人份,人均约为一半" copy in `PrintView`. The Settings UI to change it lands with #6; nothing reads a literal 2 anymore.
- Today / Planner / Print all observe `ServingsStore` so the numbers stay consistent across tabs.

## Notes
- Scaling shopping-list *quantities* by servings requires structured amounts and is deferred to #9 (amounts are free-text strings today).

Closes #4

> **Stacked PR** — based on #31 (issue #3 timer rework). GitHub will retarget this to `main` automatically when #31 merges. Merge #31 first.

## Changes
- **Background / locked screen**: `CookingTimerStore.start` schedules a `UNUserNotificationCenter` local notification at the timer's end date, with the dish + step name in the body ("清蒸鲈鱼 · 处理鱼身 的时间到了。"). Pause and reset cancel the pending notification, and restarting reschedules it.
- **Foreground**: completion plays a system alert sound (`AudioServicesPlaySystemSound`) and a success haptic (`UINotificationFeedbackGenerator`). A freshness guard skips the sound when the completion task resumes long after the fact (e.g. app was suspended — the local notification already alerted the user), preventing a double alert.
- **Permission**: requested only while `.notDetermined`, the first time a timer starts. If the user declines, timers keep working — they just don't alert in the background.
- `CountdownTimerView`/`StepPage` pass a human-readable label for the notification body.

data.body:
Closes #3

## Changes
- **New `CookingTimerStore`** (`DietExpert/DietExpert/CookingTimerStore.swift`): a shared `@MainActor` observable store holding every step timer, keyed by recipe id + step index. Timers are anchored to an absolute end `Date` instead of a decrementing counter, so remaining time is always computed from the wall clock — correct across page swipes, tab switches, and backgrounding.
- **Root cause fixed**: the old view-local `.task(id: running)` loop used `try? await Task.sleep`, so when SwiftUI cancelled the task on view disappearance, the cancelled sleep returned immediately, `try?` swallowed the `CancellationError`, and the loop spun the countdown to zero with no delay. The store's completion task checks `Task.isCancelled` explicitly.
- **`CountdownTimerView` rewritten**: renders remaining time via `TimelineView(.periodic)` reading from the store; no more view-local `@State` timer state. Start / pause / reset semantics unchanged (重置 at 0 restarts the full duration, matching previous behavior).

## Verification
- `xcodebuild` build of `DietExpert/DietExpert.xcodeproj` (scheme DietExpert, iPhone 17 simulator) passes.
- Conflict preflight: no other open PR branches.

## Note for reviewer
This is the base of a stacked pair — the follow-up PR for #4 (completion sound/haptic/notification) branches off this one. Merge this first.

## What Problem This Solves

Automation operators currently see impossible relative schedule durations such as `in 60m`, `60m ago`, `in 24h`, and `24h ago` when a job crosses a normal rounding boundary. Both `openclaw cron list` and `openclaw cron show` present these inconsistent values even though the same command already renders schedule intervals through the canonical shared duration formatter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron CLI owned a second, inconsistent duration-rounding implementation. It selected a minute/hour unit before rounding, so values that rounded up to the next unit still kept the old unit. The fix removes the duplicate rounding branches and reuses the existing `formatDurationHuman` owner, while preserving the documented `<1m` special case. Production code shrinks by 11 lines.

## User Impact

Operators see coherent `in 1h` / `1h ago` and `in 1d` / `1d ago` values in both automation list and detail views. Existing sub-minute output, ordinary durations, past/future symmetry, JSON output, scheduling behavior, configuration, and persistence remain unchanged.

data.body:
Fixes #118236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could persist isolated announce automations whose fallback delivery could never choose among multiple configured channels. The agent run would complete, but every delivery would fail later because no deterministic channel existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

CronService now owns a static create/update/declarative validation gate. Gateway supplies only the current configured channel IDs, keeping cron core plugin-agnostic. The gate rejects only isolated announce jobs with an implicit `last` channel, no preserved session route, no provider-prefixed target, no `bestEffort` opt-in, and at least two configured channels. Discovery failures accept the mutation so this check cannot create false rejections.

PATCH validation runs only when delivery resolution can change (`delivery`, `sessionTarget`, `agentId`, or `sessionKey`). Existing ambiguous jobs can still be disabled or renamed. The current service type has no independent top-level `channel` patch field; `delivery.channel` is covered by the `delivery` gate.

The issue says creation was accepted at the cited production SHA, but that source already had a Gateway-only missing-channel preflight. That preflight was broader than the requested contract, did not exempt best-effort/session-backed cases, and did not protect direct CronService or declarative callers. This change narrows Gateway to explicit-channel validation and makes the service mutation boundary canonical.

The production delta is +85 net lines, covering the injected channel-list fact, three mutation paths, PATCH compatibility ownership, Gateway delegation, and invalid-request classification. No legacy path or duplicate service policy remains.

## User Impact

On multi-channel hosts, statically ambiguous isolated announce jobs now fail immediately with configured channel IDs and actionable fixes: set `--channel <id>` or opt into `--best-effort-deliver`. Explicit channels, one-channel hosts, provider-prefixed targets, preserved session routes, and best-effort jobs continue to work.

## What Problem This Solves

The conversation-binding pilot (#118075) established the pattern: ambient module state needs a lifecycle owner. A read-only inventory of current main found 44 hand-verified sites that lack one — cross-request pending state (agent questions, conversation turns, placement claim waiters, agent-job maps with live timers, MCP grants), plus listener/registry sets that accumulate across lifecycles. Worse, the tree has a structural asymmetry: close-path owners don't run on in-process SIGUSR1 restart and restart-path owners don't run on close, so each lifecycle leaks through the other.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ownership moved to the factory instead of 44 hand-wired clears. `resolveGlobalSingleton` now accepts an owner class at slot creation:

- **close-and-restart** — clears on terminal close and SIGUSR1 restart (default for runtime state)
- **close-only** — preserves serialization tails across in-process restart where clearing a promise chain would break ordering
- **plugin-registry** — clears inside `clearActivePluginRegistry` for plugin-contributed registrations

Drain ordering is deliberate: the gateway drain runs after plugin cleanup and before secret-snapshot clearing; the SIGUSR1 drain runs before durable task reload; plugin host runtime state clears in `finally` after plugin cleanup — this also delivers the highest-value single fix from the inventory (wiring `clearPluginHostRuntimeState` into registry clearing; it was previously reachable only from the test reset).

Conversions are semantic, not just map-dropping: pending question/turn/placement waiters are rejected or settled so no promise dead-ends at shutdown; agent-job timers are canceled; MCP watchers are canceled and awaited. Sites where clearing would violate serialization or need channel-specific teardown are explicitly deferred with reasons (table in the report below).

**Named LOC tradeoff:** production +525/−118 (net +407). The growth is the semantic cancellation paths for live timers, waiters, and OS resources — the alternative (silent map clears) would trade a leak class for a dead-ended-promise class. The deleted per-site `*ForTest` resets and the removed restart/close asymmetry are the structural payback.

## User Impact

Gateway close and in-process restart now start from a clean slate: no stale pending approvals, no orphaned waiters resolving into the next lifecycle, no duplicate listener dispatch after restart, and minted MCP grants do not survive termination.

## Deferred (explicit, with reasons)

Stateful target drivers (atomic builtin-registration reset needed), task-flow registry (SQLite-backed, reloads), health registry (extension WeakSet), before-agent-reply (ALS scope, not a registry), fire-and-forget hooks (needs generation-aware cancellation), session/store/SQLite writer queues (clearing promise tails violates serialization), extension candidates (need channel/plugin teardown owners).

## Evidence

- 734 focused tests passed; 150 highest-risk rerun after final extraction
- Both core tsgo lanes; changed-file format/lint; runtime import cycles 0; madge 0; full build clean
- Structured autoreview clean

SDK surface change is additive only: resolveGlobalSingleton and resolveGlobalMap retain their existing call signatures and add optional reset and lifecycle-owner parameters with prior behavior preserved when omitted. Manifest regenerated per the gate's intentional-change flow.

## What Problem This Solves

Core had dozens of local copies of the same insertion-ordered Map trim mechanics. Those copies obscured the few caches whose eviction actually owns domain behavior, and the directory/MCP TTL caches duplicated expiry, capacity, and config-identity handling.

This change routes 85 mechanically equivalent FIFO trims through `pruneMapToMaxSize`, removes the named local wrappers, shares the TTL cache implementation, centralizes the backup hardlink cache, and gives the native hook relay retention cap one owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

`pruneMapToMaxSize` already owns the canonical Map FIFO contract, including normalized limits and empty-iterator handling. Callers retain their existing recency decisions (`delete` + `set`) and pre-insert behavior (`max - 1`) where required.

The TTL implementations had two real divergences:

- Directory cache used one active config map and expired at `age > ttl`.
- MCP used config identity per row and expired at `age >= ttl`.

The canonical cache now uses a WeakMap per config object and expires at `age >= ttl`. Scoped directory invalidation names the config explicitly; global reload still clears every config scope. Tests pin A→B→A retention, config-specific invalidation, and exact-boundary expiry.

The backup link cache remains a deliberately inert node-tar link cache: node-tar 7.5.22 consults `get(dev:ino)` before emitting a hardlink and records via `set`; suppressing both keeps every archived entry independently restorable. Fleet and general backup keep their distinct archive pipelines.

### What Problem This Solves
In Control UI Talk / voice mode, `waitForChatResult` listens for Gateway `chat` WebSocket events and concurrently issues an `agent.wait` RPC call. When `agent.wait` resolves (indicating the agent run has completed on the server), `waitForEmptyFinalFallback()` handles turns that produce no text.

Previously, `waitForEmptyFinalFallback()` scheduled an unconditional timer without coordinating event loop ticks between WebSocket frames and `agent.wait` completion. If a `chat` WebSocket event carrying assistant text arrived in a queued tick after `agent.wait` resolved, an improper timeout would resolve with `"OpenClaw finished with no text."` before the text frame could settle.

Closes #117899.

### Why This Change Was Made
By implementing event-loop tick deferral and proper event listener prioritization, `waitForChatResult` ensures:
1. Any in-flight WebSocket `chat` frame carrying assistant text immediately resolves the turn with the real assistant text.
2. A genuine empty turn (e.g. tool-only call) cleanly resolves with the synthetic `"OpenClaw finished with no text."` fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a scheduled job with `delivery.mode: "none"` reports `lastDeliveryStatus: "not-requested"` even when its agent demonstrably delivered the message.

`none` means the *runner* does not deliver — the agent sends the message itself with the `message` tool. The job-state projection treats "the runner did not deliver" as "no delivery was requested", so a job whose agent verifiably reached its target persists the same value as a job that never sent anything at all. An operator checking whether a scheduled message went out cannot tell those two apart, and `openclaw cron` shows `not-requested` for a job that did exactly what it was configured to do.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveDeliveryState` already reports real outcomes for the other mode where `requested` is false: `webhook` gets `delivered` / `not-delivered` with its error preserved. `none` just falls through to `not-requested`.

This adds the matching positive case for `none`. It needs no new evidence, because for this mode `delivered` already *is* the verified message-tool delivery — `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts:101` sets `delivered = verifiedMessageToolDelivery`, and mode `none` returns that state unchanged. So `delivered === true` is already proof the agent's own send reached the intended target, and the fix is to stop discarding it.

The change is deliberately limited to the `true` case. A `false` value here does **not** mean the send failed: for a `none` job with no explicit target the plan target is empty, so target matching cannot succeed and `delivered` is false for every send, healthy ones included. Reporting that as a failure would mark working jobs broken, so anything short of a verified delivery keeps reading `not-requested`.

## User Impact

For `delivery.mode: "none"` jobs, a verified agent send now persists `lastDeliveryStatus: "delivered"` and `lastDelivered: true` instead of `not-requested`. Every other case, and every other delivery mode, is unchanged.

## Evidence

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer-trigger.delivery-state.test.ts src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts
```

New file `timer-trigger.delivery-state.test.ts`. Against unmodified sources (`git checkout origin/main -- src/cron/service/timer-trigger.ts`):

```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

Only the verified-send case flips. The three that pass on unmodified `main` are negative controls that must not move — a `none` job that delivered nothing stays `not-requested`, `announce` stays on the requested-delivery path, and `webhook` keeps its own carve-out.

After:

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
```

The second file is the pre-existing `service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts`, unmodified — including `suppresses delivered=false when delivery.mode none opts out of delivery`, which still passes because `delivered: false` still reports `not-requested`.

Full cron suite:

```
 Test Files  165 passed (165)
      Tests  1996 passed (1996)
```

Typecheck and lint:

```
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental ...   # exit 0, no output
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service                        # exit 0, clean
```

Production diff is +13 lines in one file, four of them comment.

**Limits:**

- No live gateway run. Proof is the repo's cron suite against the real `resolveDeliveryState`, not an end-to-end scheduled job against a live channel.
- Scoped to the job-state projection. Run status and `failureAlert` are untouched.

Context, not a claim: #113181 reports a separate `delivery.mode: "none"` problem — a send that fails or returns success-equivalent without arriving. This change does not address that and is not proposed as a fix for it; that path needs failed-send evidence out of the agent runner, since every message-tool evidence surface there is populated only on success.

## What Problem This Solves

PR #118098 cleared the mechanically-safe portion of the `lint:all` baseline and reserved 40 findings for a maintainer lint-scope decision. That decision has been made and this PR executes it: `pnpm lint:all` now exits 0 with zero findings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolution by class, applying the narrowest correct treatment for each:

- **Genuine fixes** (behavior-neutral, owning tests run): error re-throws in the live-updater now carry `{ cause }` (restoration-failure precedence preserved), map-spread and control-regex findings in the changelog verifier were restructured/converted to Unicode escapes, the release-CI summary test uses `toSorted()`, and shadowing locals in the parallels model test were renamed. The pass also resolved findings that had accrued on `main` since #118098.
- **Rule allow-list**: `__typename` is the GraphQL specification's type-name introspection meta-field ([GraphQL September 2025 §4.1](https://spec.graphql.org/September2025/#sec-Type-Name-Introspection)); `_meta` is the MCP protocol's reserved metadata property/parameter ([MCP 2025-11-25 Base Protocol: `_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/index#_meta)). These ecosystem contract names, not style violations, are allowed by `no-underscore-dangle`.
- **Fixture excludes**: the exclusions cover only `.agents/skills/autoreview/tests/fixtures/**` and `test/fixtures/oxlint-boundary-guards/**`, two negative-test corpora that intentionally contain parser/lint violations. Any future finding in source outside those exact trees still fails lint.
- **Platform idioms**: the Android KaTeX calls retain the single-argument API required by the AndroidX-injected `WebMessageListener` bridge and use explained per-line disables because the unicorn rule pattern-matches browser `window.postMessage`. Origin admission is enforced once at the [`addWebMessageListener` registration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4260cbad7c8c22ab78ef5586420c2e575fab2ec5/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatMathRenderer.kt#L526-L530), which passes `setOf(KATEX_ORIGIN)`. AndroidX documents that this registration injects the JavaScript object only into frames matching `allowedOriginRules` and that the object uses `myObject.postMessage(message[, MessagePorts])`; the app's exact AndroidX WebKit 1.16.0 source archive is [here](https://dl.google.com/dl/android/maven2/androidx/webkit/webkit/1.16.0/webkit-1.16.0-sources.jar) (`WebViewCompat.java:588-596, 673-680, 786-804`; `JavaScriptReplyProxy.java:26-33, 58-60`). The renderer is byte-identical to `main` except for the two lint comments, so this is zero behavior change. Linux quickchat retains its explained `keyCode === 229` IME fallback because `event.key === "Process"` is not provably equivalent across IME stacks.

## User Impact

None at runtime. `lint:all` becomes a zero-noise gate: any future finding outside the two named negative-test corpora is a real regression.

## Evidence

- `pnpm lint:all`: exit 0, zero findings (authoritative oxlint pass; the unrelated extension-boundary prepare step hangs after child exit on this host and was skipped via `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1` — the lint pass itself is complete)
- 246 owning tests + 4 bench tests (class A), config tests (class B), 77 config/fixture tests + autoreview harness 271 passed/1 skipped (class C)
- `pnpm tsgo` + `pnpm tsgo:test` clean; changed-file formatter-equivalence check and `git diff --check` clean; structured autoreview clean
- Android runtime coverage after the corrected bridge call shape comes from this PR's `android-test-play` and `android-test-third-party` CI lanes

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Equivalence-by-construction proof for the runtime-code surfaces

The review asks for after-fix Android runtime proof of the KaTeX bridge. At head `4260cbad7c8c` the bridge cannot behave differently from `main`, because the only delta in both runtime files is lint comments. Inspectable transcript (comment-stripped SHA-256 comparison, `origin/main` vs `HEAD`):

```text
$ node compare.mjs   # strips // and /* */ comments, collapses whitespace, hashes
apps/android/app/src/main/assets/katex/renderer.js
  main comment-stripped sha256: a949777c22800982
  head comment-stripped sha256: a949777c22800982
  executable-content identical: true
apps/linux/ui/quickchat.js
  main comment-stripped sha256: defc287a1de6a5c1
  head comment-stripped sha256: defc287a1de6a5c1
  executable-content identical: true
```

Every byte the WebView executes is identical to shipped `main`; the earlier two-argument `postMessage` change is fully reverted per the AndroidX `JavaScriptReplyProxy` single-argument contract (webkit 1.16.0 sources, `JavaScriptReplyProxy.java:26-33`; origin admission at `ChatMathRenderer.kt:526-530`). Android CI lanes (`android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`) are additionally green on this exact head.

## Maintainer confirmation of the permanent lint exceptions

Maintainer decision (authorized): the two identifier allowances and two fixture excludes are intended as permanent scope, each bound to an external contract rather than concealing future findings — `__typename` is the GraphQL spec's reserved introspection field, `_meta` is the MCP protocol's reserved metadata field, and the two excluded subtrees (`.agents/skills/autoreview/tests/fixtures/`, `test/fixtures/oxlint-boundary-guards/`) exist solely to contain intentional violations for negative tests, one of which is an intentional parse error that can never lint clean. Any source finding outside those exact boundaries still fails the gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes terminal agent runs being classified differently depending on which core consumer observed the lifecycle event. In particular, a plain `AbortError` could be recorded as a timed-out task, signal-only aborted lifecycle events could appear completed in activity notes, and several task/session/chat/audit/TUI paths independently re-derived timeout and cancellation precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical terminal-outcome owner now accepts lifecycle events directly, classifies reasons once as success/timeout/cancellation/failure, and lets each owning domain map that classification into its existing vocabulary. Gateway `agent` responses deliberately retain their shipped cancellation-as-`timeout` wire contract, while internal task/session projections use cancellation. ACP background tasks now use the existing structured `TURN_TIMEOUT` detail code instead of matching human-readable error text.

The ambiguous legacy `aborted: true` event without timeout attribution is treated as cancellation. Current producers emit explicit `stopReason`/`timeoutPhase` for real timeouts; this removes the older compensation that turned every bare abort into a timeout.

AI-assisted change; I reviewed the complete implementation and behavior boundaries.

## User Impact

Cancelled runs are no longer mislabeled as timed out in task tracking, and session activity no longer reports signal-only aborted runs as completed. Existing Gateway clients continue receiving the same final `ok | error | timeout` status values.

## What Problem This Solves

Pending request and approval lifecycles had drifted across several runtimes. A node-host gateway request timer could keep a worker process alive, approval resolution or expiry could overtake a slow pending-message delivery, and plugin conversation-binding approvals could remain actionable and accumulate for the entire Gateway lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one deferred-backed pending-request registry for worker, node-host, and LSP RPCs, and one small delivery-lifecycle registry shared by both approval fanout owners. Transport policy remains local: worker socket interruption, LSP cancellation, channel rendering, and native finalization are unchanged. Worker request definitions are table-driven, and plugin binding approvals now use the previously authored domain policy of a 30-minute deadline with a 512-entry oldest-first cap.

## What Problem This Solves

PR #118110 (channel lifecycle adoption) named three gateway/consumer-boundary limitations where a recorded lifecycle fact loses to a weaker derived signal — the doctrine violation class the lifecycle series exists to remove:

1. A channel publishing durable `blocked` (terminal auth failure) had that fact replaced by gateway-owned `stopped` when its task exited: restart stayed correctly suppressed, but the operator-visible reason degraded from actionable to generic.
2. Discord's pre-gateway REST token probe discarded the HTTP status, so the channel could not distinguish 401 (terminal) from a transient failure, and mapped everything dishonestly.
3. WhatsApp's derived unhealthy projection superseded the channel-authored `conflict` health label in collected status output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each fix moves precedence to the recorded fact at its owner boundary:

- **Gateway**: terminal `blocked` is now sticky across task finalization; only an explicit channel start clears it. The finalization path no longer rewrites an actionable terminal fact into a generic stopped state.
- **Discord**: the application-ID probe returns a private discriminated result carrying the status class; 401/403 map to `blocked` + terminal disconnect, 5xx/network map to `recovering` — the same structured classification Telegram landed in #118110. The public helper contract is unchanged.
- **WhatsApp**: authored terminal health labels (e.g. `conflict`) outrank derived projections in both status collectors; raw runtime state retains both fields.

## User Impact

Operators keep the actionable diagnosis: a revoked Discord token or a WhatsApp session conflict stays visible as exactly that in `openclaw channels status`, instead of degrading to a generic stopped/unhealthy state after the task exits or the collector runs.

## Evidence

### After-fix real gateway boundary proof

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI had three clusters of drift: page-local SVG catalogs duplicated the shared Lucide icon owner, page-local formatters duplicated or obscured shared formatting contracts, and destructive actions used native browser confirms that silently fail in webviews without a dialog bridge. Nodes already carried a one-off styled workaround, so confirmation policy and lifecycle safety were split across pages.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes the existing shared owners canonical:

- Config navigation and Skill Workshop empty states now consume the shared icon catalog. Nine genuinely missing glyphs were added once; 39 page-local SVG definitions were removed.
- Workshop relative time, support-file sizes, Activity/Logs/Workboard time labels, and Usage formatter names now route through shared helpers or explicitly retain the Usage-specific fixed-precision contract.

- Sessions, Worktrees, Nodes, and dreaming actions revalidate their captured gateway/task ownership after the asynchronous decision. Nodes also abort the visible modal on connection reset, preserving the original cross-gateway safety invariant.

Destructive confirmations move from browser-native prompts to a consistent in-app modal with localized copy, safe default focus on Cancel, and accessible dialog labels/descriptions. The action semantics are unchanged, while embedded webviews no longer silently cancel these operations.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw had many keyed single-flight maps that repeated the same create/store/settle/delete lifecycle. The canonical `getOrCreatePromise` helper only supported sticky promises, so callers hand-rolled cleanup and two durable caches retained rejected promises indefinitely.

In particular, one failed CLI channel sender load poisoned both a keyed sender cache and a nested sticky lazy-runtime cache until restart. Local audio inspection likewise retained rejected probe promises until its test-only cache clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

This widens `getOrCreatePromise` with two explicit, identity-safe lifecycle policies while preserving sticky behavior for every existing caller:

- `cacheRejections: false` retains successful values but evicts the exact rejected promise.
- `evictOnSettled: true` models maps that own only in-flight work.

The CLI sender now has one keyed cache instead of two nested sticky caches. Ten clean keyed hand-rolls use the canonical helper, delivery-queue media GC uses the existing single-slot lazy loader, and three TUI refresh loops share one coalesce-plus-rerun owner.

Two surveyed sites were deliberately left alone after direct inspection: iOS approval push pending state is a cleanup projection rather than a single-flight cache, and media cleanup starts synchronously while the lazy loader starts on a microtask. Canonicalizing either would change behavior.

## User Impact

A transient channel sender load failure or rejected local-audio inspection can recover on the next request instead of requiring an OpenClaw restart. Successful cache behavior, cooldowns, LRU limits, status projections, and existing single-flight semantics remain unchanged.

Production code is net 10 lines smaller. Tests add 125 lines of regression and lifecycle coverage.
